submission.justification: No project document contains humidity-ageing data for any candidate, so the 10% transparency-loss limit is unverified for all three. R3 has the best separation (4.6 sigma at 3 cm in the 2025 summary). It is a high-index porous radiator with no stated moisture protection, so it is the riskiest option for a hard ageing requirement. R1 is porous with a hydrophobic treatment, which suggests better humidity resistance. It is the best separator among the options that plausibly meet the limit. In my scans R1 gave 3.67 sigma at 2 cm, 3.84 at 2.5 cm, 3.85 at 3 cm, 4.01 at 3.5 cm, 3.44 at 4 cm and 3.33 at 5 cm. The curve is noisy, but it is highest at 3.5 cm. R2 is only 2.9 sigma at 3 cm, and I did not simulate it. This recommendation is provisional. Before procurement, someone must run or obtain a humidity-ageing test for R1, and for R3 if it is to be reconsidered.

requirements.requirement: Best possible pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c
requirements.evidence: R1 at 3.5 cm gives 4.01 sigma in simulation. R3 gave 4.6 sigma at 3 cm in the 2025 summary and is better on this metric, but I did not confirm it against the ageing limit.
No document gives ageing data for any candidate. R1's hydrophobic treatment is only indirect support. The vessel is flushed with dry nitrogen, which also does not prove compliance.

requirements.requirement: Radiator is one of the three candidates
